content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand the Apple Sports app, broadening its football coverage while also offering tennis fans a new way to track some of the most important tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds multiple football leagues and tennis draw functionality

When the Apple Sports app first launched, the experience was quite limited both in terms of regions supported and sports covered.

Since then, the app has continued to evolve on both fronts — expanding to over 170 countries and regions while continuously adding support for new sports, leagues, and events.

For example, earlier this year Apple Sports rolled out to 90 new countries and introduced a series of new features centered around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports updated again, adding Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier League to its football lineup.

In addition, Apple says the app can now let tennis fans "track draw results in real time... including draws for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," and users can also "see the matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Here is the full update content for Apple Sports 4.4:

Football coverage continues to expand with the addition of Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League, and the South African Premier League. Tennis fans can track draw results in real time on Apple Sports, including draws for Grand Slams and 1000-level events. See the matchups and results for each round at a glance.

Are you using Apple Sports? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
